test_cases.description: Verify that spec/cli.py declares its root Click group using cls=AgentFoxGroup instead of the bare @click.group() decorator.
preconditions: agentfox.io module is installed and importable
test_cases.input: Import the root CLI group object from spec/cli.py
test_cases.expected: The root group object's class is AgentFoxGroup (i.e., type(root_group) is AgentFoxGroup)
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: from spec.cli import cli; assert type(cli) == AgentFoxGroup OR isinstance(cli, AgentFoxGroup)

test_cases.description: Verify that spec/cli.py contains no manual banner rendering or config loading code after migration.
test_cases.input: Read the source text of spec/cli.py
test_cases.expected: Source contains no calls to manual banner rendering functions or manual config loading that predated AgentFoxGroup adoption
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: source = read_file('spec/cli.py'); assert 'render_banner' not in source; assert manual_config_load_pattern not in source

test_cases.description: Verify that _json_error_exit() and _error_type() helper functions have been removed from spec/cli.py.
test_cases.input: Read the source text of spec/cli.py
test_cases.expected: Neither '_json_error_exit' nor '_error_type' appear as definitions or calls in spec/cli.py
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: source = read_file('spec/cli.py'); assert '_json_error_exit' not in source; assert '_error_type' not in source

test_cases.description: Verify that when AF_AGENT=1 is set, the spec CLI suppresses banner output and routes errors through the AgentFoxGroup JSON error handler.
test_cases.input: Invoke `AF_AGENT=1 spec --help` or any valid spec subcommand
test_cases.expected: No banner text is written to stdout or stderr; any error is emitted as a JSON object
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: result = run_cli(['spec', '--help'], env={'AF_AGENT': '1'}); assert 'banner' not in result.stdout.lower(); assert 'banner' not in result.stderr.lower()

test_cases.description: Verify that any unhandled exception propagating to the root group is formatted as a JSON error envelope with a non-zero exit code.
preconditions: A subcommand can be triggered to raise an unhandled exception (e.g., by patching internals)
test_cases.input: Invoke a spec subcommand that raises an unhandled RuntimeError
test_cases.expected: stdout contains a JSON object with 'ok: false' or an error field; process exits with non-zero exit code
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: result = run_cli_with_exception_trigger(['spec', 'render']); parsed = json.parse(result.stdout); assert parsed['ok'] == false; assert result.exit_code != 0

test_cases.description: Verify that spec render --json wraps markdown output in a render envelope with ok, format, content, and sections fields.
preconditions: A valid spec with all artifacts (requirements, test_spec, tasks) exists on disk
test_cases.input: Invoke `spec render --json --combined` for a valid spec
test_cases.expected: stdout is a JSON object containing ok=true, format='markdown', a non-empty content string, and a sections array
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: result = run_cli(['spec', 'render', '--json', '--combined']); parsed = json.parse(result.stdout); assert parsed['ok'] == true; assert parsed['format'] == 'markdown'; assert 'content' in parsed; assert 'sections' in parsed

test_cases.description: Verify that spec render --combined --json returns a single merged content string in the envelope.
preconditions: A valid spec with multiple artifacts exists on disk
test_cases.input: Invoke `spec render --json --combined` for a spec with requirements, test_spec, and tasks
test_cases.expected: stdout JSON has a single 'content' string (not an 'artifacts' map) containing merged markdown, plus a 'sections' array
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: result = run_cli(['spec', 'render', '--json', '--combined']); parsed = json.parse(result.stdout); assert 'content' in parsed; assert 'artifacts' not in parsed; assert isinstance(parsed['content'], str); assert parsed['sections'] == ['requirements', 'test_spec', 'tasks']

test_cases.description: Verify that spec render --json without --combined returns per-artifact content under an 'artifacts' key.
preconditions: A valid spec with requirements, test_spec, and tasks artifacts exists on disk
test_cases.input: Invoke `spec render --json` without --combined flag
test_cases.expected: stdout JSON has ok=true and an 'artifacts' map with keys for each artifact; no single 'content' key
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: result = run_cli(['spec', 'render', '--json']); parsed = json.parse(result.stdout); assert parsed['ok'] == true; assert 'artifacts' in parsed; assert 'content' not in parsed; assert 'requirements' in parsed['artifacts']

test_cases.description: Verify that spec render without --json outputs raw markdown to stdout with no JSON wrapping.
preconditions: A valid spec exists on disk
AF_AGENT environment variable is not set
test_cases.input: Invoke `spec render` without any --json flag
test_cases.expected: stdout is raw markdown text; json.parse(result.stdout) raises a parse error
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: result = run_cli(['spec', 'render']); assert result.exit_code == 0; assert json_parse_fails(result.stdout); assert result.stdout.strip().startswith('#') OR is_markdown(result.stdout)

test_cases.description: Verify that spec render uses emit_ok from agentfox/io/ to construct all JSON envelopes.
test_cases.input: Read the source text of spec/cli.py and inspect the render command implementation
test_cases.expected: The render command calls emit_ok (imported from agentfox.io) for all JSON output; no direct json.dumps or click.echo(json...) calls are present in the render handler
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: source = read_file('spec/cli.py'); assert 'emit_ok' in source; render_section = extract_render_handler(source); assert 'json.dumps' not in render_section; assert 'click.echo' not in render_section OR render_section has no json output

test_cases.description: Verify that spec validate emits a structured error object with category='schema', artifact, path, message, and value fields for schema check failures.
preconditions: A spec artifact file exists with a known schema violation (e.g., malformed requirement ID)
test_cases.input: Invoke `spec validate` on a spec containing a schema error
test_cases.expected: stdout JSON has valid=false; errors array contains at least one object with category='schema', non-empty artifact, path, message, and value fields
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: result = run_cli(['spec', 'validate', '--spec', 'bad_schema_spec']); parsed = json.parse(result.stdout); assert parsed['valid'] == false; schema_errs = [e for e in parsed['errors'] if e['category'] == 'schema']; assert len(schema_errs) > 0; err = schema_errs[0]; assert 'artifact' in err; assert 'path' in err; assert 'message' in err; assert 'value' in err

test_cases.description: Verify that spec validate emits a structured error object with category='integrity', check, message, and requirement_id for integrity check failures.
preconditions: A spec with a known integrity violation exists (e.g., a requirement with no test cases in test_spec)
test_cases.input: Invoke `spec validate` on a spec with an integrity error (missing test case coverage)
test_cases.expected: stdout JSON errors array contains at least one object with category='integrity', non-empty check, message, and requirement_id fields
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: result = run_cli(['spec', 'validate', '--spec', 'integrity_violation_spec']); parsed = json.parse(result.stdout); integrity_errs = [e for e in parsed['errors'] if e['category'] == 'integrity']; assert len(integrity_errs) > 0; err = integrity_errs[0]; assert 'check' in err; assert 'message' in err; assert 'requirement_id' in err

test_cases.description: Verify that spec validate returns {valid: true, errors: []} when validation completes with no errors.
preconditions: A fully valid spec artifact set exists on disk with no schema or integrity errors
test_cases.input: Invoke `spec validate` on a fully valid spec
test_cases.expected: stdout JSON is {valid: true, errors: []}; process exits with code 0
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: result = run_cli(['spec', 'validate', '--spec', 'valid_spec']); parsed = json.parse(result.stdout); assert parsed['valid'] == true; assert parsed['errors'] == []; assert result.exit_code == 0

test_cases.description: Verify that spec validate returns valid=false and a non-empty errors array with exit code 1 when validation finds errors.
preconditions: A spec artifact set with at least one error exists on disk
test_cases.input: Invoke `spec validate` on a spec with validation errors
test_cases.expected: stdout JSON has valid=false and errors is a non-empty array of structured error objects; exit code is 1
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: result = run_cli(['spec', 'validate', '--spec', 'invalid_spec']); parsed = json.parse(result.stdout); assert parsed['valid'] == false; assert len(parsed['errors']) > 0; assert result.exit_code == 1

test_cases.description: Verify that spec validate uses emit_ok or emit from agentfox/io/ to write validation result envelopes.
test_cases.input: Read the source text of the validate command handler in spec/cli.py
test_cases.expected: The validate handler calls emit or emit_ok (from agentfox.io) and does not use click.echo(json.dumps(...))
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: source = read_file('spec/cli.py'); validate_section = extract_validate_handler(source); assert 'emit_ok' in validate_section OR 'emit' in validate_section; assert 'click.echo(json.dumps' not in validate_section

property_tests.description: For any invocation of spec render --json, the stdout JSON object always contains 'ok' and either 'content'+'sections' (combined mode) or 'artifacts' (per-artifact mode), never omitting these top-level keys.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate arbitrary valid spec definitions (varying number of artifacts: 1-3, arbitrary markdown content lengths 0-10000 chars); run spec render --json and spec render --json --combined for each
property_tests.invariant_check: parsed = json.parse(stdout); assert 'ok' in parsed; if combined_mode: assert 'content' in parsed AND 'sections' in parsed; else: assert 'artifacts' in parsed

property_tests.description: For any error object in the errors array returned by spec validate, every error object contains a non-empty category field whose value is one of 'schema', 'integrity', or 'io'.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate spec artifact files with varying combinations of schema errors (wrong ID format, missing fields), integrity errors (uncovered requirements), and IO errors (missing files); run spec validate for each combination
property_tests.invariant_check: parsed = json.parse(stdout); VALID_CATEGORIES = {'schema', 'integrity', 'io'}; for err in parsed['errors']: assert 'category' in err; assert err['category'] in VALID_CATEGORIES; assert len(err['category']) > 0

property_tests.description: For any invocation of the spec CLI with AF_AGENT=1 or --json, every byte written to stdout is part of a valid JSON object with no interleaved plain-text, banners, spinners, or raw markdown.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate arbitrary spec invocations (subcommands: render, validate, status; with AF_AGENT=1 or --json flag; valid and invalid spec inputs) using hypothesis or equivalent property-based testing framework
property_tests.invariant_check: result = run_cli(cmd, env={'AF_AGENT': '1'}); stdout_text = result.stdout.strip(); if stdout_text: for line in stdout_text.split('\n'): if line.strip(): json.parse(line)  # must not raise ParseError

property_tests.description: Static analysis of spec/cli.py shows zero occurrences of _json_error_exit, _json_error_exit(), and click.echo(json.dumps after migration.

property_tests.invariant_check: source = read_file('spec/cli.py'); assert '_json_error_exit' not in source; assert 'click.echo(json.dumps' not in source

edge_case_tests.description: Verify that spec render --json emits a JSON error envelope with ok=false when the spec file does not exist or cannot be read.
preconditions: The target spec file does not exist on disk
edge_case_tests.input: Invoke `spec render --json` referencing a non-existent spec file
edge_case_tests.expected: stdout is a JSON object with ok=false and an error message; exit code is 1; no raw traceback is printed
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: result = run_cli(['spec', 'render', '--json', '--spec', 'nonexistent_spec']); parsed = json.parse(result.stdout); assert parsed['ok'] == false; assert 'error' in parsed; assert result.exit_code == 1

edge_case_tests.description: Verify that spec render --json omits missing artifacts from the artifacts map and includes a warnings array noting the omission.
preconditions: A spec exists that has requirements and test_spec but no tasks artifact
edge_case_tests.input: Invoke `spec render --json` on a spec missing the tasks artifact
edge_case_tests.expected: stdout JSON has ok=true, artifacts map without the 'tasks' key, and a warnings array mentioning the missing artifact
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: result = run_cli(['spec', 'render', '--json', '--spec', 'no_tasks_spec']); parsed = json.parse(result.stdout); assert parsed['ok'] == true; assert 'tasks' not in parsed['artifacts']; assert 'warnings' in parsed; assert any('tasks' in w for w in parsed['warnings'])

edge_case_tests.description: Verify that spec validate emits a structured IO error with category='io' when an artifact file is missing or unreadable.
preconditions: A spec directory exists but one or more artifact JSON files are missing or have no read permissions
edge_case_tests.input: Invoke `spec validate` on a spec with an unreadable or missing artifact file
edge_case_tests.expected: stdout JSON has valid=false; errors array contains an object with category='io', artifact filename, and descriptive message; exit code is 1
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: result = run_cli(['spec', 'validate', '--spec', 'missing_artifact_spec']); parsed = json.parse(result.stdout); assert parsed['valid'] == false; io_errs = [e for e in parsed['errors'] if e['category'] == 'io']; assert len(io_errs) > 0; err = io_errs[0]; assert 'artifact' in err; assert 'message' in err; assert result.exit_code == 1

edge_case_tests.description: Verify that a structured error object for a top-level error omits the path and value fields rather than including null values.
preconditions: A spec artifact has a top-level schema error (not field-specific) that produces a structured error without a jsonpath
edge_case_tests.input: Invoke `spec validate` on a spec with a top-level (non-field-specific) error
edge_case_tests.expected: The relevant error object in the errors array does not contain 'path' or 'value' keys at all (not null, but absent)
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: result = run_cli(['spec', 'validate', '--spec', 'top_level_error_spec']); parsed = json.parse(result.stdout); err = find_top_level_error(parsed['errors']); assert 'path' not in err; assert 'value' not in err

edge_case_tests.description: Verify that importing StatusSpinner from spec.ui after deletion raises an ImportError at runtime.
edge_case_tests.input: Execute `from spec.ui import StatusSpinner` in a Python interpreter
edge_case_tests.expected: Python raises ImportError with a message indicating spec.ui module is not found
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: try: exec('from spec.ui import StatusSpinner'); assert false, 'Should have raised ImportError'; except ImportError as e: assert 'spec.ui' in str(e) OR 'No module named' in str(e)

edge_case_tests.description: Verify that output produced before AgentFoxGroup initialization is suppressed or deferred to prevent mixed plain-text before the JSON stream.
preconditions: A module-level side effect that might produce output exists (or is simulated)
edge_case_tests.input: Invoke a spec subcommand with AF_AGENT=1 in an environment where module-level initialization would occur
edge_case_tests.expected: No plain-text appears before the first JSON object on stdout; entire stdout parses as valid JSON lines
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: result = run_cli(['spec', 'render'], env={'AF_AGENT': '1'}); lines = [l for l in result.stdout.strip().split('\n') if l]; for line in lines: json.parse(line)  # each line must be valid JSON

smoke_tests.description: End-to-end smoke test: agent calls spec render --json --combined and receives a valid render envelope with merged markdown content.

mockable: agentspec rendering logic (can return fixture markdown)
